articles.title: Origin raises $20 million to scale general-purpose construction robots
articles.summary: Origin emerged from stealth with $20 million in funding to scale OG-1, a general-purpose interior construction robot for tasks such as wall finishing, sanding and priming. The company is deploying robots on job sites and preparing large-scale pilots with customers in the US and Europe, targeting labor shortages, project delays and productivity constraints in construction.

articles.title: From Approval to Abuse: Privilege Escalation Attacks on Harness-Protected Coding Agents
articles.summary: The paper identifies a privilege-escalation risk in coding agents that use execution harnesses and user-approved allow-rules to manage permissions. Adversarial content planted in a repository can steer agents into requesting overly broad permissions, which, once approved, can enable silent malicious actions without further human oversight. The authors report successful allow-rule elicitation in 58% of experimental instances across platforms including Claude Code and Codex CLI.
articles.advisor_relevance: This matters because enterprise adoption of agentic coding tools depends on trust, governance, and secure workflow controls. The findings suggest that current human-approval mechanisms may not be sufficient, creating potential demand for stronger AI security, permission management, and developer-tool governance solutions while also highlighting risks to rapid deployment of coding agents in production environments.

articles.title: OliO: ODE-based Linear Transition Operator for Self-Supervised Time Series Forecasting
articles.summary: The paper introduces OliO, a self-supervised time series forecasting method that uses an ODE-based linear transition operator to model temporal flows in latent representations. The approach is designed to improve stability and long-term dependency modeling, with reported MSE reductions of up to 5.75% versus strong baseline methods across benchmarks.
articles.advisor_relevance: This is an early-stage technical research paper rather than a commercial deployment or company-specific development.
